hints: Look at the formula and options, all four are alcohols, so focus on whether each one is primary, secondary or tertiary.
Remember that acidified dichromate(VI) oxidises primary and secondary alcohols but leaves tertiary alcohols unchanged, so one option can be ruled out straight away.
Think about what type of alcohol you get when you reduce a carboxylic acid with LiAlH4, and use that to decide between a primary alcohol and a secondary alcohol.
walkthrough:
**Recognise Q is an alcohol**

The formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$ with the structures shown tells us Q is a butanol isomer. Let us classify each one.

A: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ is secondary, B: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ is primary, C: $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_3\text{COH}$ is tertiary, D: $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{OH}$ is primary.

**Use the oxidation clue**

Primary alcohols oxidise to aldehydes then carboxylic acids, secondary alcohols oxidise to ketones, tertiary alcohols resist oxidation.
$$\text{primary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{aldehyde} \rightarrow \text{carboxylic acid}$$
$$\text{secondary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{ketone}$$
$$\text{tertiary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{no reaction}$$
Since Q can be oxidised, it cannot be tertiary, so option C is out.

**Use the LiAlH4 reduction clue**

Reduction of a carboxylic acid with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ gives a primary alcohol only, because the $\text{-COOH}$ carbon becomes a $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ carbon.
$$\text{RCOOH} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} \text{RCH}_2\text{OH}$$
Q cannot be made this way, so Q cannot be a primary alcohol. That rules out B and D.

**Conclude the structure**

Only the secondary alcohol remains. It fits both clues perfectly, as it oxidises to butan-2-one but cannot be formed by reduction of a carboxylic acid.

options.A: Butan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol. It is oxidised by acidified potassium dichromate(VI) to the ketone butan-2-one, and it cannot be made by LiAlH4 reduction of a carboxylic acid, which only gives primary alcohols.
options.B: Butan-1-ol is a primary alcohol so it is oxidised, but it CAN be made by reducing butanoic acid with LiAlH4 ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ to $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$). This fails the second condition.
options.C: 2-methylpropan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol. The carbon bearing the OH has no hydrogen, so it resists oxidation by acidified dichromate(VI). This fails the first condition.
options.D: 2-methylpropan-1-ol is a primary alcohol so it is oxidised, but it CAN be made by reducing 2-methylpropanoic acid with LiAlH4. Students choosing this forget that branched primary alcohols are still primary alcohols.
